items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the round-feedback form after the sprint-47 live clicks); filed by Claude
items.title: Roads are a tree plus a detour test, and only villages above a size spur: no lattice, and round 6's tail inside 35 s
items.design:
MOVED (2026-10-07, the sprint 49 close-out; Ben: place by subject): sprint 49 -> 50. SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): the village spur floor is 40,000 heads (the ladder's ~p90; median road pass 18 s loaded, 1 of 16 seeds under 10 s), size read as the population step's headcount; a border link ends ONLY on a town or a spurring village (LOGISTICS.md § 4). The street carpet is not this item's: BL-1130 (centres consolidate) thins the centres upstream, and this item's "no lattice on the densest seed" is read after it.

ROUND 2 (the lane's own findings and the settle review): fix the floor at 40,000 as the constant; border endpoints restricted to towns and spurring villages; road_generation.cpp's two hand-written cache clears (~616-619, ~689-691) replaced by invalidate_logistics_caches so the new nearest-anchor field is never missed; the loading bar's roads weight (hard_coded_world.cpp ~495, 38,000 ms) and kBorderUnitsPerNation re-measured; road_generation_harness's "R2 highway tier reachable when qualified" FAILS on 0 of 8 seeds, identically on b03fd52e -- find why (the percentile gate, the two-major-endpoints rule, or the harness's qualified regen) and fix the cause or split it to its own item with the reading; never weaken the row.

SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): BL-1077 (village roads cost) is FOLDED IN. Its target joins this done-when: generate_roads under ~10 s Release on the library seeds, read after the spur floor; if the floor alone does not reach it, BL-1077's bound (one multi-source search per centre, or a shared reach field, digest-neutral by itself) is this item's second step. THE 35 s IS JUDGED ON THE WHOLE TAIL, jointly with BL-1117 (settle tick one), which joins the sprint with its fix: on seed 0 the settle is ~56 s Release, tick 1 alone 38.5 s, so roads alone cannot meet it.

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, walking round 6: "we also need many fewer roads... it should be heavily discouraged to build a lattice of roads"; he chose the tree plus a detour test over "no second path", and spurs only for villages above a size). LOGISTICS.md § 4 carries the rule; STARTUP.md § Round 6 carries the 35 s target.

THE WORK. (1) Replace the relative-neighbour redundancy edges with the DETOUR TEST: after the Kruskal MST, a candidate link between two centres is laid only when the network's route between them costs more than 2x the direct A* route (one constant, named). The percentile rationing of loops applies to the loops the test admits (a delegated reading that keeps BL-618/BL-621 intact; Ben may overturn). (2) A village lays a spur only above a size floor, MEASURED on the 16 curated seeds first (Rule 0b: road tiles, spur count and pass time per floor candidate). (3) The border link rule is unchanged.

A WORLD-MOVER: every road digest and the sweep pins move -- read road tile counts, pass time (gen_step_costs --finish) and the haulage baseline (memory: goldens cannot see trade) on the 16 seeds before and after, then ONE re-bless.

DONE WHEN. No lattice on a capture of the densest seed; road pass time and tile count recorded old -> new per seed; round 6's tail lands within 35 s of arrival on seeds 0 and 28 in Release (gen_step_costs); one re-bless; road_generation_harness green (connectivity held). CARRIED to sprint 49 at the sprint 48 close (2026-10-04): owed R4 a quiet Release gen_step_costs run on 16 seeds (road tiles and pass time per seed, old -> new, against ~10 s); R6 an isolated haulage reading of this change (or fold into BL-1165); R7 a cold review of round 4 (8b921ee6, directed paths).

items.author: Claude (the sprint 49 close-out; Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07)
items.title: A built processor gets its inputs: 85% running and at most 5% input-starved at handoff
items.design: TARGETS RAISED (Ben, 2026-10-08): G1 >= 85% running at handoff, plus G1b <= 5% input-starved (now, or decommissioned after starving), 16 seeds. 70% had no recorded reason beyond a first stretch from a 17.6% baseline; G1 alone counts a plant idled for want of a buyer as failure, so starvation gets its own target. CARRIED from sprint 49 (Ben, the close-out form, 2026-10-07: close with G1 unmet, carry it to sprint 50 as a logistics item). The 16-seed market_viability reading on main after BL-1183 C1: G1 54.7% of built processors running at handoff against Ben's 70% (G2 54.4 and G3 88.9 pass). About a quarter of built processors are already decommissioned by the handoff, and by their last reported state almost all were input-starved (half A: 578 of 674). Diagnose which inputs fail to arrive, at which markets, and why - no producer within reach, a producer whose surplus is not dispatched, or a dispatch the margin refuses - then fix the cause in the network or dispatch, not by clamping the loss reflex. Re-measure construction stalls here too: whether a stalled site is ever abandoned (BL-1183 C3) is still unruled. Judge it on the market-viability skill, 16 seeds.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50, deferred by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: Long-term viability: plants running at handoff are still running at play tick 50
items.design: DEFERRED from sprint 50 (Ben, 2026-10-09: 'push the long term viability work for another sprint, after the various other gameplay loops are settled'). Target carried: G1 at tick 50 >= 85% (market-viability; reported, not gated, in sprint 50). FOUND (starve_trace_probe, f98d43df, shipped code before sprint 50's wave 2b): of 665 plants lost handoff->t50, 386 starved. (1) STEEL: a background-firm CONSTRUCTION BOOM - on 33 starving markets 725 sites draw steel at t50, 701 background-owned (ports/hubs 264, food 181, fuel 79); site need ~373/tick vs processors ~35; making builds read steel scarcity is a NEW AI GRANT (raise it). (2) UNDELIVERED HAULS: copper ore - dispatcher 'would send' in 36/47 cases, arrivals ~8/tick; split Logistic Points cap / one-destination-per-pass / goods sent elsewhere (SUPPLY/LOGISTICS). (3) POOL-HELD STOCK: 42 plants starve while stock sits unlisted in other pools at the market; split processor reservation vs sell-order floor (MARKETS). (4) FUEL->PROPELLANT COLD START: with generation bounded by want, neither chain stands at generation and no launchpad exists on any seed; space access depends on settle/play building both (PRODUCTION, ERAS gate). Ruled healthy, keep: fair-price ceiling (cf off: -8.0 G1t50), background pull (cf off: -1.4), households' first draw. Re-measure with the probe after sprint 50 merges before designing.

items.author: Claude (sprint 50 PROPELLANT cold review; backlogged by Ben 2026-10-09)
items.title: A rival's launch fuel is not drained by its own scorer or the space programme - or it is, by ruling
items.design: BACKLOGGED by Ben (2026-10-09, launch fuel form) - both questions open, for a ruling when space access matters. Context: MARKETS.md step 4 reserves a pad pool's propellant from auto-surplus (Ben 2026-10-09; may still be sold by a standing order). Cold review of the PROPELLANT lane found three rival paths that ignore that reservation: (a) corp_ai.cpp listable_surplus (~2572) uses processor_reservation, so the trade candidate places an uncapped sell order that empties the pad pool, re-placed each time stock rebuilds; (b) the scorer's directed dispatch (~2735) has no reservation and can haul pad propellant to the capital market on the same body; (c) space_programme.cpp (~140-175) buys 50-unit lumps from the pool holding most unreserved stock - pad pools are now where propellant piles up. Q1: should the scorer sell/haul only above the pad reservation? Q2: should the space programme buy only the excess? No seed had a launchpad at t50 in sprint 50, so the effect is latent.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16 playtest); filed by Claude
items.title: A road is an edge between two tiles, not a property of one
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16 playtest): 'Roads should be directional, so they always cross the edge of two tiles.' RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): roads move to EDGES, as rivers already are - not a rendering-only change. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Roads - an edge between two tiles) and RENDERING.md (Roads draw across the edge they cross). Grain: a tier per hex side, six sides, two bits each (0 none / 1 Track / 2 Road / 3 Highway), both tiles of an edge carrying it as both tiles of a river crossing do, side i mirroring side i+3. The road multiplier moves from the node to the EDGE in logistics.cpp edge_cost, beside the river discount that already lives there (A* keeps its 4-cardinal walk and its hex_side_for_offset derivation). Every count of roaded TILES becomes a count of roaded EDGES, each edge once: Logistic Points, network upkeep, reach, interdiction. Placement names a tile AND a side. Pre-v53 saves migrate by laying, between each pair of 4-cardinal neighbours that both carried a road, an edge at the LOWER of their two tiers. World save v53 claimed. A WORLD-MOVER: measure haulage_measure --far-trade and market_viability before and after; a re-bless is Ben's. BRIDGES GRANTED (Ben, 2026-10-17): "edge means from one tile centre to another, but not only one tile centre. This should allow spanning water with bridges" / "Roads can go over water with bridges no problem." So a road edge is permitted where EITHER END is water, and a run of such edges across a strait IS a bridge - no second mechanism, no new field. A bridge edge prices as its tier, and a crossing made on one is paid at that road price rather than the water sea-leg price. What stays forbidden is only the original target: a road that is a property of ONE tile. This unblocks the four road_generation_harness rows the build left red (R6a markets off the backbone, R6b/R6d trunk links stamping nothing, R2s-a) and the 15 markets stranded off their nation backbone. HAULAGE ACCEPTED (Ben, 2026-10-17): the far-trade drop (pooled window Y units -28%, share past the nearest market +2-5 points) is the intended meaning - a road discounts only the crossing it covers - so no re-tune; re-measure after bridges land, since they change it again. COLD REVIEW 2026-10-17: do-not-merge, eight findings, fix round sent. Save seam, mirror invariant across every writer, count_road_edges sides-0-2 and the wire seam all judged correct and unbreakable. The eight: place_road side inserted before tier so five 5-arg calls read tier as side (logistics_harness T10 and building_upkeep R11f red, neither run); stamp_edge returns true having laid nothing, which is the mechanism behind the 15 off-backbone markets and needs no design call; two of six sides can never be crossed by a 4-cardinal walk yet auto_road_side and the street loop offer them, so a road can be bought, counted and billed while crossing nothing - RULED in LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Only a side a walk can cross may carry a road), the field stays six-wide and the restriction is on what may be written; body_reach_field lost the road discount entirely so roads no longer shorten reach and corp_ai scores a road that buys nothing; lane_clock hop_cost lost it too so a convoy clock drifts against its own priced path; network_upkeep bills nothing where the canonical half is unowned land, about half of frontier roads by grid orientation, and count_road_edges has no production caller so the verified function is not the one that runs; a UI neighbour-signature bit collision hides a sea lane when survey flips; corp_ai can now buy 18 edges on one tile instead of 3. Also noted: every pre-v53 save loses its isolated village streets on load, which is the ruled migration, so it stands - the lane is reporting how many tiles it drops.

items.title: A later round's reroll can move an earlier round's committed draws, through the viability attempt index
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found verifying BL-1339, 2026-10-16). planetology.cpp's comment on the three preference streams claims 'bumping a later round's reroll counter cannot disturb an earlier round's already-committed draw'. That is FALSE: resolve_preferences folds the rejection attempt index k into all three streams (ra/rb/rc), so a Life roll that changes how many attempts the world needs moves the SYSTEM draws too. Observed by tools/verify/life_reroll.cpp: campaign seed 0 roll 7 resolves at attempt 2 and theta moves 1.519 -> 1.462, plate count 9 -> 8; seed 7 roll 3 resolves at attempt 3. Pre-dates BL-1339 (it was already true of the three Life draws) and is only now measured. THE CALL IS BEN'S: either the System draws become attempt-independent (so an accepted round really is committed), or the doc and the comment stop claiming independence. A doc and the code disagree, so one of them is wrong and the fix is work.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the market attraction form); filed by Claude
items.title: A tile clears at the market it is most attracted to: logistics cost over the centre's pull, not grid distance
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "Markets should be mildly dynamic, where each tile has a market attraction for each market, based on logistics distance to that market centre and also a modifier for that market centre which can come from either tech nodes or buildings." DESIGNED: MARKETS.md section Catchment is an attraction, not a distance; LOGISTICS.md section 3b (the off-road leg); GLOSSARY Market attraction. Today market_for_tile is nearest centre_tile by SQUARED GRID DISTANCE, column wrapped (market_clearing.cpp:165-284), cached in an unsaved raster rebuilt on market-set change - it cannot see a road, a tech or a building. New: attraction = traversal cost (LOGISTICS.md section 1) / centre pull, lowest wins, ties to the lowest market id; pull is a modifier_set multiplier, 1 by default. OFF-ROAD (Ben's call): a tile with no roaded edge costs the nearest roaded tile's network cost PLUS off-road-per-tile x the 4-cardinal step count to it (column wrapped), so every tile belongs to a market and far land drifts between markets as roads approach. Reach (section 3) is NOT changed - catchment and permission stay separate. CADENCE (Ben's call): recompute on change - a road laid or cut, a pull gained or lost, a market carved or folded - never on a clock, so it stays a pure function of standing state and is still never saved. A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability and haulage_measure --far-trade before and after; a re-bless is Ben's. Sequenced after BL-1340 (roads are edges), which changes what a roaded tile is. SAME-NATION BONUS (Ben, 2026-10-16): a tile owned by the same nation as the centre is 1.2x as attracted to it - a property of the (tile, centre) PAIR, not of the centre, so a centre pulls harder only on its own ground. Written into MARKETS.md. Measure how many tiles actually change hands at 1.2: the bonus is small against the cost spread, so report the count of tiles whose market flips because of it, per seed, and say so if it flips almost none.

DESIGNED: PRODUCTION.md section A building needs a road; LOGISTICS.md section 4 (Generation roads every building site). A tile carries a road when any of its hex sides carries a roaded edge - a crossing INTO the tile is a road ON it, from either side. EXTRACTION IS NOT EXEMPT (Ben's call): a remote deposit is worked only once a road reaches it, which with BL-1348 means a chain of crossings built out to it one tile at a time - the intended cost of far ore. GENERATION IS BOUND TOO (Ben's call): the road pass lays a crossing to every site it stamps, so the 1960 world holds no building the rule would refuse; exempting generated buildings would make the opening world the one place the rule fails. Add the refusal to placement_rules.cpp beside the stack and ceiling checks, with a message that names the road. A WORLD-MOVER and a playability shift (roads gate all expansion): measure market_viability, haulage_measure --far-trade and the generated building count before and after. Sequenced after BL-1340.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16: "we can take a look at generation to make sure logistics producing assets give points across each nation"); filed by Claude
items.title: Verify that generation's seeded logistics sources really cover every nation
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16: "we can take a look at generation to make sure logistics producing assets give points across each nation"). CORRECTION, 2026-10-16: an earlier revision of this item claimed a landlocked nation has NO Logistic Points because corporation_generation's building mixes seed ports but no inland hub. The mixes do lack the hub (corporation_generation.cpp:305, the hub appears only as a placement score at :449) - but a DEDICATED pass seeds them: seed_logistics_sources (logistic_points.cpp:382) places inland_logistics_hubs at world fold until every consumer on a nation's ground has coverage 1 and every pool meets claim x k_pool_margin (2.0), bounded by k_max_hubs 4000 over 64 sufficiency rounds, siting a hub on the serving market's centre_tile where that is on the nation's dry ground and on the consumer's own tile otherwise. So coverage is engineered by construction, and this item is MEASUREMENT, not new work. THE WORK: measure per nation on the curated seeds - sources seeded by network, tiles covered, pool made against claim, and how many nations fall back to on-consumer-tile hubs rather than market centres. That also tests Ben's picture (a centralised capital with high points, diminishing with distance, extended by outlying hubs): if hubs land mostly on consumer tiles rather than at centres, the picture will not appear however the lens is drawn.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the logistics visibility message); filed by Claude
items.title: Two unrelated Logistic Point systems are live at once, and the lens and marches read the retired one
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found mapping Ben's 2026-10-16 logistics message). THE ROOT CAUSE of what Ben saw in play. Two LP systems stand in the tree: (1) THE REAL ONE, BL-1309, src/world/logistic_points.*: a pool per NATION made only by inland hubs (120/tick), railway stations (150) and ports (120), scaled by each source's upkeep supply, with a bounded-Dijkstra reach field per (nation, network, body) that is full strength to lp_full_reach {6,10,12} then fades to zero over lp_fade_length {6,8,8}; consumed ONLY by production (lp_need = 10 x workforce run), granted pro-rata or by the nation's share rule, and spent as a labour multiplier so half the points means half the output. (2) THE LEGACY ONE, BL-596, active_lp_anchor_pools in logistics.cpp:1075: a flat 20/tick pool at every ANCHOR, where collect_anchor_tile_set (:31) seeds an anchor at EVERY population centre plus every port and hub - no falloff, no nation, no rail. Marching units still draw the legacy pools (economy_system.cpp:4210-4300, first-come in unit-id order). THE THROUGHPUT LENS READS ONLY THE LEGACY ONE. So Ben's reading that cities supply logistics is true of the system he can SEE and false of the one that runs the economy - the doc already ruled 'Cities make none' (2026-10-14). THE WORK: one system. Retire the legacy anchor pools, move the march draw onto the nation pool (the march is the priced consumer - LOGISTICS.md's 'Active lands first' and 'Armies claim first' need re-reading against a model where trade draws nothing at all), and point the lens at the real model (BL-1353). RECONCILED 2026-10-16: do NOT delete the passive-LP remains - Ben ruled the same day that a shipment draws points again (BL-1361), so market_lp_left (supply_system.cpp:1035, returns 0), market_component::trade_lp_spare (permanently 0, serialised at save v46, read by corp_ai) and corp_command rejected_no_lp are REVIVED by that item, not retired. Retire only the legacy ANCHOR pools and the march path that reads them.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the logistics visibility message); filed by Claude
items.title: The throughput lens: per-tile point numbers, the player's own nation only, no taglines, and roads recoloured in the pass that already redraws them
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "let's change the throughput lens, we can drop the '(active logistics points)' taglines, and give a number to each tile, so we can see exactly how many points we have. The lens should also be player facing, so we can see only the player's home nation's road network and points... instead let's recolour the roads to be a brighter white." TAGLINES: overlay.cpp:59 ('Throughput (active Logistic Points)') and the on-canvas legend title at body_surface_canvas.cpp:1490, which also prints 'anchor: N LP/tick' and 'N anchors - N LP/tick total'. PER-TILE NUMBERS: none today - the wash is the REACH-COST field (1 - sqrt(rc/p90)), not LP at all, and the only LP-valued mark is an anchor ring whose share is always exactly 1.0 because the legacy rate is uniform. LENSES.md:1020-1030 argues per-tile LP cannot vary for that reason; BL-1309 overtook that argument and nobody revisited it, since lp_coverage_at (logistic_points.cpp:342) is already a per-tile function and resolve_logistic_points already yields per-building coverage and grant fractions. Note the lens currently suppresses the hover card body-wide (:6058) as 'a value field with no structure grain' - that premise also goes once the field carries real per-tile numbers. PLAYER-FACING: no owner or nation filter exists anywhere in the path - collect_anchor_tile_set and body_reach_field are both body-wide. Filter to the player's home nation, and reconsider the suppressed border band (:3978) once it is one nation's network. ROADS, AND THE RENDERING ANSWER: the second road pass Ben noticed is real and deliberate - route_drawn goes true under this lens alone (:4216-4217), redrawing the network as vector curves over the baked road paint. Recolouring is CHEAP there: change the three IM_COL32 literals at :4224-4226 (track/road/highway) to the brighter white and leave the bake alone. The static-stroke cache key already includes overlay (:4484), so a lens toggle rebuilds strokes, never pixels. Do NOT try to brighten the BAKED asphalt per lens: bake_params carries no lens field and region_hash keys only tile fields, so adding one would re-bake every visible chunk on every lens toggle. Re-run tools/verify/throughput_field_census.cpp (LENSES.md:1043 requires it whenever the anchor set moves) and scripts/verify/throughput_lens.lua.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the logistics visibility message); filed by Claude
items.title: Tile selection gains a Logistics section: the points provided here and the points consumed here
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "we should improve visibility by giving tile selection a surface for logistics. We should show the number of logistics points provided, and the number consumed by that tile." Attach in COLUMN 3, the Tile card, right after the 'Tile [x, y] - <road tier>' title row and before the building grid (selection_panel.cpp:2999-3001) - already the tile-grain, road-aware spot, and a BeginChild that scrolls on its own. A fifth column would break SELECTION.md's four-column ruling (Ben, 2026-10-13); the disabled Supply action button is the cheaper alternative if the card proves too tight. EVERY FIGURE IS ALREADY IN SCOPE at that draw site: the economy_report gives report.logistic_points - per building need / coverage / granted / class, and per nation pool / made[3] / sources[3] / claim[3] / granted[3] / rule_set - and w is non-const there, so lp_coverage_at(w, memo, tile_id) gives the coverage a building on this tile WOULD get even with nothing built, which is the one genuinely per-tile figure. PROVIDED = what a source on this tile makes (its network rate x its upkeep supply scalar, 0 where no source stands); CONSUMED = the sum of its buildings' granted points, with their need beside it so a shortfall reads as a shortfall. Say which nation's pool it draws on, since every building on a nation's ground draws that nation's pool whoever owns it. A live click is owed.

(1) The 'What it is' section still declares LP 'is BIFOLD' with a passive/active table and 'Cities generate it.' items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
items.title: A tile requests the points it needs and they are routed to it over one path, split across sources in distance order
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16, on the LP form: "Both: surfaces now, routing straight after"). DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section How a tile's points get to it. SEQUENCE IS BEN'S: BL-1352 (one system), BL-1353 (lens) and BL-1354 (tile surface) land FIRST, so routing is measured against honest numbers rather than guessed - the real model's reach already fades with distance and extends with outlying hubs, and nobody has yet seen it drawn. THE MODEL: today there is no routing at all - a nation-wide scalar pool scaled by a per-tile reach field (max over the nation's three networks), granted pro-rata or by the share rule. New: a tile's request is the sum of its buildings' needs; it is filled over ONE best path, never two at once; a source fills part of a request only if it both reaches the tile AND is itself connected back toward the market centre (Ben: "further sources have to both reach the tile, and produce enough to extend backward towards the market centre"), so points arrive along a chain the centre anchors and an isolated hub supplies nothing; where the nearest source falls short the remainder comes from the next nearest that satisfies both tests, in distance order. This supersedes the older constraint-2 rule that a draw lands on exactly one anchor. SCARCITY (Ben's ruling): distance ORDERS the queue and never raises the bill - requests inside the falloff range are served first, then those beyond, and a far building draws the same points as a near one. The settled rule 'the draw is what moves, not how far' therefore stands; NR-620 measured a 73% convoy-traffic collapse the one time a distance draw was tried, so any implementation that makes a far building cost more points is wrong by ruling, not by taste. MARCHES (Ben's ruling): a march draws the nation pool and competes with production. RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): the march CLAIMS FIRST, keeping his 2026-09-24 ruling (NR-917) literally now that its other half is gone - it arbitrated armies against trade, and trade draws nothing, so a march is supplied before the production behind it. Written into LOGISTICS.md. Determinism: allocation must stay order-independent - a deterministic priority over a sorted set, never first-come by iteration order (the march draw is first-come in unit-id order today, economy_system.cpp:4210). A WORLD-MOVER: measure market_viability, haulage_measure --far-trade and per-nation output before and after.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
items.title: A road may always be built across a national border, and never further
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "if another nation holds the market centre, we may not be able to even build roads to supply LP. So due to this case, it should always be possible to build a road over a national border, but not further." DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section 4 (A road may always cross a national border). From a tile you hold, one crossing into a neighbour's tile is always permitted; that foreign tile is not then a tile you may build FROM, so the road stops where it lands - a connection, never a corridor. It is the exception that keeps BL-1348 (a road is laid from a road) from making a foreign-held market centre unreachable, which under BL-1356 would make every tile behind it unsuppliable. Sequenced after BL-1340 and BL-1348, whose placement rule it amends.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
items.title: The player can construct a market centre, at a high cost in materials
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "We also want to give the player a way to construct market centres, this can just be a high cost for the materials needed. This should help to reduce the number of tiles pulled towards neighbouring markets." DESIGNED (shape): MARKETS.md section A market centre can be built. Expensive in materials and gated by nothing else - the cost IS the constraint. A rival nation may build one too, by the same verb, so it is not an asymmetric player power. Still to settle: the material bill, whether a new centre must stand a minimum distance from an existing one, and what it does to the spontaneous-emergence pass (MARKETS.md section Spontaneous market emergence) which already creates centres on its own. Needs the verb on the corp_command seam with an ACTIONS.json entry, and the surface to press it.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16, the Logistic Points form); filed by Claude
items.title: Generation starts a market centre with several levels of logistics building
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): "I imagine we might start generation with multiple levels in logistics buildings at the market centre." RULED (Ben, 2026-10-16): SEVERAL HUBS STACKED, not a tier ladder - generation puts more than one hub building on the centre tile. The stack rule already permits it (2-12 in aggregate, PRODUCTION.md section Building stacks) and a hub already makes a flat 120 points a tick scaled by its upkeep supply, so this is seeding, not new mechanism: seed_logistics_sources (logistic_points.cpp:382) already sites hubs at the serving market centre_tile where the ground allows and adds them one at a time until coverage and pool margin are met - it should start a centre with several. Gives Ben's picture: a centralised capital with a high number of points, diminishing with distance, extended by outlying hubs. Report points made at the centre against an outlying tile, per nation.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16); filed by Claude
items.title: A better road carries points further: Track 6, Road 8, Highway 10, fading to zero at double; rail carries 20 and delivers only where it connects
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): 'let's add an extension bonus to higher tiered roads. So tracks reach 6 tiles, roads reach 8, and highways reach 10 tiles. Railways can reach 20 tiles, but they only supply the exact tile they connect to.' RULED: those are FULL-STRENGTH distances and the fade runs to ZERO AT DOUBLE them (Ben, 2026-10-16) - track 6/12, road 8/16, highway 10/20. DESIGNED: LOGISTICS.md section One pool. THE ROAD HALF IS A RECALIBRATION, not new mechanism: lp_full_reach[road] is 6 with per-tier step costs lp_road_step {_, 1.0, 0.7, 0.5}, which already yields 6 / 8.6 / 12 tiles - set the steps to 1.0 / 0.75 / 0.6 for 6 / 8 / 10, and lp_fade_length[road] = lp_full_reach[road] for the double-distance fade. THE RAIL HALF IS NEW BEHAVIOUR: lp_full_reach[rail] 10 -> 20, and delivery becomes point-to-point - the station's points land on the tile the line connects to and on no tile the line merely passes, which is the rule goods already obey (board and leave only at stations, section 4c). Sea is untouched and keeps 12 full / 8 fade; say so rather than quietly generalising the double-fade to it. Measure coverage per nation before and after, then market_viability and haulage_measure --far-trade.

items.author: Ben (2026-10-16); filed by Claude
items.title: A shipment draws Logistic Points again, by cargo quantity, at the anchor it leaves
items.design: SPRINT 55 (Ben, 2026-10-16): 'we need to consider how trading consumes logistics points' - RULED the same day: yes, a shipment draws again. The cap was retired in BL-1309's cut and the code still stands, zeroed: market_lp_left (supply_system.cpp:1035) returns 0.0f, commit_trade_shipment (:1083) voids the pools and the refusal, market_component::trade_lp_spare is permanently 0 yet serialised at save v46 and still read by corp_ai's rival-Marketplace estimate, and corp_command::rejected_no_lp serves a gate that draws nothing. REVIVE rather than rewrite, and note BL-1352 was going to delete exactly this code - it has been reconciled. THE DRAW: cargo quantity at the anchor the shipment leaves - the settled formula, what moves and not how far, so it does not reintroduce the distance draw NR-620 measured at a 73% convoy-traffic collapse. NEVER REFUSED WHOLE: a trade is a standing route with nobody to tell, so the shipment sends what the anchor admits (SUPPLY.md section A shipment); whole refusal is for COMMANDED legs only (Ben, 2026-10-05, NR-969). Ordering: the march claims first (NR-917, which with trade drawing again recovers its original subject), then trade and production. A WORLD-MOVER on the traffic itself: haulage_measure --far-trade is the measurement that matters, against the 1055/802 and the 13,954/11,277 baselines, plus market_viability G1/G1b for input starvation.

items.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1342..BL-1344, 2026-10-16)
items.title: The construction panel still cannot see the sim's pro-rata rationing, because the sim never publishes its realised build rate
items.design: SPRINT 56 (found delivering BL-1342, 2026-10-16). BL-1342 made the UI read what run_construction reads - inventory, the capacity row, the fair-price ceiling, state_idle - and closed the lying ETA. ONE DIVERGENCE REMAINS BY DESIGN: BL-1209's plan_short_shelves pre-solves a pro-rata allocation across every site contending for one shelf, in visit order, and the UI does not duplicate that solver. So where several sites compete for the same shelf the panel reads OPTIMISTIC, never pessimistic. The right close is not a second copy of the solver: run_construction should publish each site's REALISED rate in economy_report, and the panel should read it, keeping one source of truth. That is economy_system.* and was outside the UI lane's owned files. Then the mirror can be deleted outright rather than kept in step.

items.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1342..BL-1344, 2026-10-16)
items.title: A construction progress bar wobbles because its denominator is re-priced live
items.design: SPRINT 56 (found delivering BL-1343, 2026-10-16). Progress is construction_paid / construction_capex(...), and capex is re-priced from live market prices and the live site multiplier, so the bar can move backwards when prices rise or the reach/stack field changes. The ticks ratio has the same flaw through construction_site_multiplier. The drift-free fix is to store the original total on the building when construct_for sets ticks_remaining, which is a persistent field and therefore a save-format bump - deliberately NOT taken inside BL-1343. Cheap, and it also gives the queue an honest 'cost left'.

items.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1342..BL-1344, 2026-10-16)
items.title: Every placement refusal but the launchpad collapses into "invalid tile", so the toast misnames a full stack
items.design: SPRINT 56 (found investigating BL-1341, 2026-10-16). construct_building maps every can_place_in_world refusal except launchpad_exists into construction_result::invalid_tile (construction.cpp:213), so a full extraction stack, a full non-extraction stack and a full province ceiling all report 'invalid tile' in the post-hoc toast - a tile that is perfectly valid. The build-door row is honest (BL-1341 gave it the real wording and the numbers); it is the seam's own result enum that is lossy, and the seam is also the AI-facing one, where a wrong reason is a wrong signal. Carry the placement_reason through instead of flattening it.

items.author: Claude (found delivering BL-1365, 2026-10-17)
items.title: The rail rows are the one non-grid row left in the build list, a four-line box among one-line rows
items.design: SPRINT 55 (found delivering BL-1365, 2026-10-17). Every construction row is now one line in a fixed-column grid (construction.md: One line a row / The line is a grid). draw_rail_rows lives in src/ui/rail_tool.cpp, which was outside that lane's owned files, so the Track and Railway Station rows still draw a four-line bordered box - and they now sit visibly taller between the one-line Infrastructure rows above and below them (see the lane's construction_build_door_extraction.png capture). The lane passed them their OLD metric so they are not clipped, which is the right holding action and not the end state. THE WORK: bring both rail rows into ui::construction_grid's columns and the shared hover card, reusing construction_row_height / construction_row_hovered / construction_row_card / construction_grid_bar rather than a second idiom. Note BL-1255's live click asked for the track row to be restyled like the road rows, which this subsumes.
